ip_top_stories.title: GEMA wins copyright lawsuit against Suno in major AI music ruling
ip_top_stories.summary: German performing rights society GEMA has won a landmark copyright infringement case against AI music generator Suno, with the court ruling that AI models built on copyrighted material without authorisation are not protected under law. The decision has significant implications for AI music companies, as it establishes that training on copyrighted works without consent or payment is unlawful under German law. Multiple outlets have covered the ruling, which GEMA described as a victory for creators' rights.

ip_top_stories.title: Legal experts weigh in as Delhi HC extends fair dealing to cover AI training in ANI-OpenAI case
ip_top_stories.summary: India's Delhi High Court has extended the fair dealing doctrine to cover AI training data in the ANI versus OpenAI case, a ruling that legal experts say exposes significant limits in existing copyright law. A deputy minister has separately stated that AI training using copyrighted works requires owners' approval, highlighting a policy tension. The ruling is drawing international attention as courts globally grapple with AI training and copyright.

ip_top_stories.title: South Korea Ends AI Music Copyright Ban With Disclosure-First Registration Standard
ip_top_stories.summary: South Korea's KOMCA has lifted its ban on AI-assisted songs, replacing it with a disclosure-first registration standard under which AI-assisted works are eligible for copyright registration provided human creativity is sufficiently involved. False filings now risk royalty holds and contract termination. The move marks a significant shift in how a major music market is handling AI-generated content.

ip_top_stories.title: "An Icon of Distrust": Publishing Industry Turns Its Back on Generative AI as Labor and Copyright Disputes Mount
ip_top_stories.summary: A new report finds the publishing industry is increasingly rejecting generative AI amid growing labour and copyright disputes, with authors, publishers and rights holders hardening their stances. The piece documents rising industry-wide distrust of AI tools and the unresolved intellectual property questions underpinning that sentiment. The story reflects a broader cultural and commercial shift in how the book trade is responding to AI.

ip_top_stories.title: The Underappreciated Third U.S. Fair Use Factor in Copyright Infringement Cases Concerning AI Training
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal analysis examines the frequently overlooked third fair use factor — the amount and substantiality of the copyrighted work used — in the context of AI training data cases in the United States. The piece argues this factor may carry greater weight than courts and commentators have so far acknowledged. The analysis is relevant to ongoing U.S. litigation involving AI developers and rightsholders.

ip_further_links.title: Why is Anthropic destroying books? | Kathryn James
ip_further_links.summary: An opinion piece examines Anthropic's reported practice of destroying physical books used in AI training, raising questions about the legal and ethical implications for copyright and authors' rights.

ip_further_links.title: Huaxia Publishing House: "Annotated Books Strictly Prohibited for AI Training"
ip_further_links.summary: A Chinese publisher has taken a firm public stance against its annotated books being used for AI training, signalling growing assertiveness among rights holders in China over AI data use.

ip_further_links.title: From Consent to Control: Fragmented Consent in AI Voice Cloning
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis explores how consent frameworks are failing to keep pace with AI voice cloning technology, raising unresolved questions about performer rights and intellectual property protections.

ip_further_links.title: You trained the AI. Big Tech got paid
ip_further_links.summary: An opinion piece argues that creators whose work was used to train AI models have received no compensation while technology companies have profited, framing the issue as a fundamental inequity in the AI economy.

ip_further_links.title: EU begins enforcing AI Act transparency rules - Industry Report: European Policy
ip_further_links.summary: The EU has begun enforcing AI Act transparency requirements, with implications for AI companies' obligations to disclose training data and comply with copyright-related provisions.

ip_further_links.title: India's AI copyright ruling exposes limits of existing law
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of the Delhi High Court's AI training fair dealing ruling highlights how existing Indian copyright law is ill-equipped to address the complexities of AI-generated and AI-trained content.

ip_further_links.title: Ministry reviews copyright laws to balance AI innovation and creator protection
ip_further_links.summary: A government ministry has announced a review of copyright legislation aimed at finding a balance between enabling AI innovation and protecting the rights of human creators.

ip_further_links.title: The Published Voice: Whose Voice Are We Really Reading?
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines questions of authorial voice and attribution in the age of AI-assisted writing, raising implications for academic and trade publishing norms.

ip_further_links.title: Nvidia faces shareholder suit over AI training and 'fraudulent scheme'
ip_further_links.summary: Nvidia is facing a shareholder lawsuit alleging the company engaged in a fraudulent scheme related to AI training practices, adding to the growing body of litigation surrounding AI and intellectual property.

ip_further_links.title: SCCA's student chapter debate spotlights AI copyright
ip_further_links.summary: A student chapter of the SCCA has held a debate focusing on AI copyright issues, reflecting growing engagement with AI intellectual property questions in academic and professional communities.
